claims.statement: The invitation guide consists solely of includes for invitation-URL enablement and an invitation warning. These dependencies must be reviewed separately; this file alone does not describe access restrictions, invitation safety or actual invitations, and neither included artifact inherits a review receipt.

Turning an optional assignment deadline into a cutoff is described as removing student write access after it passes unless an extension is granted. Deadline alone is not cutoff enforcement; extension changes applicability. The linked extension procedure and actual access transition remain separately unverified.

Protected assignment paths are optional markers for grading-sensitive or otherwise noneditable-intent files. Student edits produce a submission label for teacher investigation, not a write prohibition or immutable grading files. Pattern examples define star filename matching, recursive double-star, single-character question mark, character/range sets and backslash escaping; these are shell-glob-like descriptions, not a verified matcher implementation.

The autograding guide includes the previously reviewed overview and a grading-method dropdown fragment that remains a separate dependency. Test parameters include name, commands, inputs, outputs, timeout and points; saving and adding/editing/deleting tests are configuration steps, not actual test execution, safe command approval or adequate grading. Linked parent sections are not inherited review.

Individual assignments are coursework per student with an intended no-help-from-other-students completion model. Intent does not establish enforcement, academic-integrity evidence, accommodation policy or a universal ban on other permitted support.

Assignment repositories may be public or private; the source's claim that only the student/team sees private feedback must remain in classroom context, not certify exclusion of teachers, organization admins or other privileged access. Student admin privileges are a deliberate optional choice when administrative tasks are intended, not a default grant; linked visibility/role pages remain separate evidence.
